ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram, the upper left side is resistor R1, and the upper right side is resistor R2; the two are connected in series in the upper wire. The connection point of R1 and R2 leads downward to terminal a, and the right-end node of R2 leads downward to terminal b, so if a capacitor is connected between a and b, the capacitor is in parallel with R2. At the bottom are the power supply E and switch S; after the switch is closed, a single series loop containing the internal resistance r of the power supply, R1, and R2 is formed. Reasoning: After S is closed, the total resistance is r+R1+R2=0.5 Ω+5.5 Ω+12.0 Ω=18.0 Ω, so the power-supply current I=E/(r+R1+R2)=12 V/18.0 Ω=0.667 A, approximately 0.67 A. After the capacitor is connected, in the steady state the capacitor branch is equivalent to an open circuit for direct current, and the loop current is still 0.667 A. The capacitor is connected between a and b and is in parallel with R2, so the steady voltage Uab equals the voltage across R2: Uab=IR2=(0.667 A)(12.0 Ω)=8.0 V. The capacitor charge Q=CUab=(200×10^-6 F)(8.0 V)=1.6×10^-3 C.

method.method_draft: First read the circuit topology from the image: after switch S is closed, the source E with internal resistance r drives a single loop containing R1 on the upper left and R2 on the upper right in series. Point a is the junction between R1 and R2, and point b is connected to the right end of R2, so a capacitor connected between a and b is in parallel with R2. From the text, use E=12 V, r=0.5 Ω, R1=5.5 Ω, R2=12.0 Ω, C=200 μF. For part 1, add the series resistances r+R1+R2 and use I=E/(r+R1+R2). For part 2, after a long time the capacitor branch is open for DC, so the loop current remains the same as in part 1. The stabilized capacitor voltage equals the voltage across R2, Uab=IR2, and the charge is Q=CUab.

method.method_draft: Use a Thevenin/open-circuit-voltage viewpoint for terminals a-b. From the image, identify that terminals a and b are exactly the two ends of R2, while R1, R2, r, the source, and switch S form one closed loop when S is closed. From the text, take E=12 V, r=0.5 Ω, R1=5.5 Ω, R2=12.0 Ω, and C=200 μF. First find the closed-loop current through the supply by treating all three resistances r, R1, and R2 as the loop load: I=E/(r+R1+R2). Then find the Thevenin voltage seen at a-b before attaching the capacitor, which is the voltage division share across R2: Vth=E R2/(r+R1+R2). In the final DC state, the capacitor connected at a-b charges until its voltage equals this open-circuit/Thevenin voltage, so Q=CVth.
